countries.name: France
countries.blurb: A country that changes character every few hours of driving — Atlantic cliffs, Alpine passes, Mediterranean heat, and a capital that rewards wandering.
countries.uniqueness: France packs a dozen distinct climates and cuisines into one country, connected by fast trains. The south runs warm and dry, the north cool and grey, and the Alps keep their own calendar — which means the right month depends entirely on which France you're going to.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: 15–22°C, gardens open, museums quiet. Lavender isn't out yet, but the Loire and Dordogne are at their greenest and prices haven't peaked.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Often above 30°C in the south. Lavender blooms in Valensole through June and July, coastal towns are full, and prices peak. Paris empties of Parisians in August.

seasons.label: Early autumn
seasons.note: Widely considered the sweet spot — warm sea, wine harvest under way, calmer streets. September in particular balances weather against crowds.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Cheapest flights and rooms. Alsace Christmas markets run through December, the Alps open for snow, and city museums are at their least crowded.

activities.title: Walk the Louvre before the tour groups arrive
activities.description: The world's most-visited museum is a different place in its first hour. Entry is timed, and the least-crowded rooms are often the ones furthest from the Mona Lisa.

activities.title: Watch the light change at Sainte-Chapelle
activities.description: Fifteen metres of 13th-century stained glass wrapping a single upper chapel. Sunny late mornings put the most colour on the stone.

activities.title: Stand on the D-Day beaches in Normandy
activities.description: Omaha, Utah, Juno and the cliffs at Pointe du Hoc, with the American cemetery above. Long, quiet, wind-blown stretches of coast that carry their history plainly.

activities.title: Cross to Mont-Saint-Michel at high tide
activities.description: A medieval abbey stacked on a tidal island off the Normandy coast. Tide tables decide whether it stands on sand or in water — the difference is dramatic.

activities.title: See the cave paintings near the Dordogne
activities.description: Some of the oldest known art in Europe sits under the limestone of the Vézère valley. Original caves are strictly limited; several are shown through exact replicas.

activities.title: Château-hop through the Loire Valley
activities.description: Over 300 châteaux across one valley — Chambord for scale, Chenonceau for its arches over the river, Villandry for the gardens.

activities.title: Follow the wine harvest in Burgundy or Bordeaux
activities.description: Late summer into autumn, whole villages turn to picking. Many estates open their doors, and the roads smell of fermenting fruit.

activities.title: Eat your way through a Provençal market morning
activities.description: Cheeses, honey, olives, herbs and knife-sharpeners under plane trees. Most markets run one or two mornings a week and are packed up by lunch.

activities.title: Sit down to a long lunch in Lyon
activities.description: The bouchons of Lyon serve the unfussy end of French cooking — quenelles, andouillette, pralines — in rooms that haven't changed much in decades.

activities.title: Taste Champagne where it's made
activities.description: The chalk cellars under Reims and Épernay run for kilometres. Houses range from grand names to small growers who'll sit and talk.

activities.title: Stand in the lavender at Valensole
activities.description: The Provence plateau turns purple in early summer. Bloom timing shifts each year with the weather, and fields are working farms, not parks.

activities.title: Drive the Verdon Gorge
activities.description: Limestone walls above turquoise water, with pull-offs the whole way round. Kayaks and pedalos launch from the lake at the western end.

activities.title: Ride the cable car under Mont Blanc
activities.description: The Aiguille du Midi lift climbs to 3,842m for a face-on view of the massif. Weather closes it often; clear mornings are the reliable window.

activities.title: Walk a stage of the Tour du Mont Blanc
activities.description: The full circuit takes ten days across three countries, but single stages from Chamonix give you the high passes without the commitment.

activities.title: Ski or hike the Alps out of Chamonix or Annecy
activities.description: Winter brings some of Europe's longest verticals; summer turns the same slopes into trails and paragliding launches above Lake Annecy.

activities.title: Cycle the vineyard lanes of Alsace
activities.description: Flat, well-signed routes link half-timbered villages between Strasbourg and Colmar, with tasting rooms roughly every few kilometres.

activities.title: Swim the calanques near Marseille
activities.description: White limestone inlets dropping into clear water, reachable on foot, by kayak or by boat. Summer fire risk closes some trails at short notice.

activities.title: Take the coast road along the Côte d'Azur
activities.description: The corniches between Nice and Menton stack three roads at three heights, each with a different view of the same sea.

activities.title: Ride Paris by night on the river
activities.description: The Seine boats run late, and the city's monuments are lit until around 1am. It's the cheapest way to see the whole centre in an hour.

activities.title: Wander Strasbourg's Christmas markets
activities.description: One of Europe's oldest, running through Advent across several squares, with Alsace's food and mulled wine and a lot of cold air.

activities.title: Do nothing in a village square
activities.description: A coffee, a newspaper you can't read, and an hour watching a place go about its day — arguably the most French thing on this list.

countries.name: Japan
countries.blurb: Dense, quiet, precise, and far stranger than the postcards — a country where a bullet train drops you at a thousand-year-old pilgrimage trail.
countries.uniqueness: Japan runs on seasons more than most places: what's worth seeing shifts week by week, tracked nationally. Blossom moves north for a month; autumn colour moves south for two. And volcanic geology means over 2,000 natural hot springs, most of them in small towns rather than resorts.

seasons.label: Cherry blossom
seasons.note: Tokyo and Kyoto peak roughly 28 March–3 April, later further north. Spectacular, but the busiest and most expensive weeks of the year.

seasons.label: Late spring
seasons.note: Widely rated the best all-round month — mild, dry, green, and far calmer than blossom season.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Hot and humid with a rainy spell in June; festival season, and the only window for climbing Fuji. Hokkaido stays comfortable.

seasons.label: Autumn colour
seasons.note: Koyo starts in Hokkaido in September and reaches Kyoto and Tokyo from mid-October into November. Second-busiest season, and worth it.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Powder snow in the north, quiet temples in Kyoto, and the best time for onsen — steam and snow together.

activities.title: Walk a stage of the Kumano Kodo
activities.description: Pilgrimage trails through the Kii Peninsula walked for over a thousand years, linking mountain shrines. The Nakahechi route is the classic; the Iseji sees a fraction of the traffic.

activities.title: Soak in a riverside onsen at Kawayu
activities.description: Hot water rises through the riverbed itself. In winter the river is dammed to make a single enormous open-air bath.

activities.title: Bathe your way around Kinosaki
activities.description: A hot-spring town of seven public bathhouses, walked between in a yukata and wooden sandals under willow-lined canals.

activities.title: See the steam vents at Beppu
activities.description: More than 2,000 hot springs in one town, including the 'hells' — thermal pools too hot to enter, plus mud and sand baths that you can.

activities.title: Take the waters at Kusatsu
activities.description: High in the Gunma mountains, with enormous volumes of hot water cooled by hand in wooden channels in a display locals have done for generations.

activities.title: Stay a night in a ryokan
activities.description: Tatami floors, futons laid out while you're at dinner, and a multi-course kaiseki meal built around what's in season locally.

activities.title: Watch morning prayers at Sensō-ji
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest temple, in Asakusa. Early morning belongs to people who actually pray there, before the approach fills with stalls and crowds.

activities.title: Walk the forest path to Meiji Shrine
activities.description: A hundred thousand donated trees planted around a shrine in central Tokyo. Weekend mornings often bring traditional wedding processions.

activities.title: Take the temple circuit in Kyoto
activities.description: Kiyomizu-dera's terrace, the vermilion tunnels at Fushimi Inari, the moss and raked gravel of the Zen gardens. Early or late avoids the worst of it.

activities.title: See Nara's deer among the temples
activities.description: Sika deer roam freely around Tōdai-ji and its enormous bronze Buddha, an hour from Kyoto or Osaka.

activities.title: Sit under the blossom at a hanami party
activities.description: Parks fill with tarps, food and quiet celebration for the two weeks the trees hold. Some shrines light the trees after dark.

activities.title: Chase the autumn colour south
activities.description: Koyo works down the country over two months — Hokkaido first, Kyoto's maples last. Temple gardens are built around the display.

activities.title: Cross the island of Naoshima by bike
activities.description: A small Seto Inland Sea island turned over to contemporary art — Tadao Ando concrete museums, a Kusama pumpkin on the pier, and old houses rebuilt as installations.

activities.title: Stand at Shibuya Crossing at rush hour
activities.description: Several thousand people crossing at once, several times an hour. The upper floors of the surrounding buildings are where you actually see the pattern.

activities.title: Eat standing up at a market counter
activities.description: Tsukiji's outer market and Kyoto's Nishiki are lined with single-dish stalls — grilled scallops, tamagoyaki, tuna cut in front of you.

activities.title: Find a six-seat izakaya
activities.description: The small alleys — Omoide Yokocho, Golden Gai, Pontocho — hide bars with room for a handful of people and a menu on the wall.

activities.title: Take a soba or sushi class
activities.description: Hands-on sessions run in most cities, usually a couple of hours, usually ending with eating what you made.

activities.title: Ride the shinkansen with Fuji on the right
activities.description: Tokyo to Kyoto in a bit over two hours. Sit on the right leaving Tokyo and watch for Fuji roughly 40 minutes in, on clear days.

activities.title: Climb Mount Fuji overnight
activities.description: The official season is short and the mountain is busy within it. Most climb through the night from a mid-mountain station to reach the crater for sunrise.

activities.title: Ski the powder in Hokkaido or Nagano
activities.description: Some of the most consistent snowfall anywhere, with onsen at the bottom of the runs and monkeys bathing in them near Nagano.

activities.title: Ferry through the Seto Inland Sea
activities.description: Slow boats between small islands, olive groves and art sites, on a stretch of water dotted with several hundred islands.
